spans.s: girayaḥ (pl.) (“the mountains,” personif.). § 615u (Skanda): IX, 45, 2556 (gave companions to Skanda).
Giriśa^2, name of a bow. § 592 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 23, 1041 (among the bows held by the five Draupadeyas).
Girigahvara, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 375 (in the north-east).
Girikā, the wife of Vasu Uparicara. § 75 (Vasu): I, 63, 2371 (daughter of the mountain Kolāhala and the river Śuktimatī).--§ 76 (Matsya): I, 63, 2373, 2377, 2384.
Girirāja = Himavat: VIII, †4321 (ºvāsinaṃ, i.e. the Kulinda prince)

Girivraja, the capital of the Māgadhas. § 11 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 409.--§ 273 (Rājasūyārambhap.): II, 14, 627 (Jarāsandha confined the defeated kings in his capital G.).--§ 275 (do.): II, 19, 762 (from G. Jarāsandha threw a mace against Mathurā).--§ 277 (Jarāsandhavadhap.): II, 21, 800 (protected by five mountains), 810; 24, 937, 951 (Kṛshṇa, Arjuna, and Bhīma came to G., Bhīma slew Jarāsandha, and the confined kings were liberated).--§ 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1091 (at G. Bhīma vanquished the son of Jarāsandha). --§ 589 (Droṇābhishekap.): VII, 4, 120 (?ºgatāś cāpi Nagnajitpramukhā nṛpāḥ, vanquished by Karṇa).--§ 717b (Nārāyaṇīya): XII, 340, 12961 (the capital of Jarāsandha). --§ 723 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 6, 333 (there Dhundhumāra fell asleep). Cf. Rājagṛha.
Girivrajeśvara (“the Lord of Girivraja”) = Daṇḍadhāra: VIII, †696.
